# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 PCAP Analysis

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; all findings below are derived directly from packet analysis via tshark.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (Intel_03:54:82) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (NetBIOS LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `plucero` from 10.8.15.133 to DC 10.8.15.4) |

## Malware Family
**GootLoader** — attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no AV/IDS alert artifact was provided; the call is based on matching documented GootLoader TTPs observed directly in the traffic):
- SEO-poisoned/typosquat delivery site serving a ZIP disguised as a legal/invoice document, containing a single-line, heavily obfuscated multi-megabyte `.js` file named like an invoice.
- Stage-2 payload retrieved with `bitsadmin`/BITS (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` User-Agent) rather than the browser.
- Persistent HTTP beaconing to a hardcoded raw IP on port 80 using a stale, non-genuine User-Agent (`MSIE 6.0`/`.NET CLR 1.0.3705`), with hex-encoded request/response bodies mislabeled as `text/html` — a long-documented GootLoader C2 fingerprint.

## Attack Timeline
| Time (local, +04:00) | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:10:58 | Victim GETs `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (104.21.55.70) → HTTP 200, `application/octet-stream`, actually a ZIP archive extracting to `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` |
| 04:11:59 | Victim (UA: `Microsoft BITS/7.8`) fetches `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` → PE32+ x86-64 DLL payload |
| 04:13:00 – 04:42:25 | 308 recurring HTTP GET/POST requests from 10.8.15.133 to `72.5.43.29:80` at path `/`, UA `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`, hex-encoded payloads — ongoing C2 beaconing |
| (same session) | TLS connection with SNI `business.checkfedexexp.com` to 172.67.170.159 |

Legitimate/benign background traffic also observed (not part of the intrusion): Windows NCSI check to `www.msftconnecttest.com`, Windows Update BITS delivery via `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `oneocsp.microsoft.com` OCSP check, and Adobe ARM update check (`acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt`).

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — raw-IP HTTP C2, hex-encoded GET/POST beacon to `/`

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 104.21.55.70) — FedEx-typosquat delivery domain
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 172.67.170.159) — same typosquat infrastructure

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — GootLoader JS-in-ZIP dropper
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — second-stage DLL payload

**Transferred files / hashes**
| File | Size | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (extracted from the ZIP served by quote.checkfedexexp.com) | 6,990,020 bytes | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL, x86-64) fetched from 72.5.43.29 via BITS | 159,232 bytes | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

## Recommendation
Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) immediately, reset the `plucero` domain account credentials, block `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, and `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter/DNS, and hunt for `wscript.exe`/`bitsadmin.exe`/`regsvr32.exe` execution chains and scheduled-task persistence on the host given GootLoader's known post-exploitation behavior.
